name: ModQuad
description: ModQuad is the first flying modular robot that can dock and self-assemble in midair. The structure is composed of agile flying modules that can easily move in a three-dimensional environment. Each module is based on a quadrotor platform within a cuboid frame, which allows it to attach to other modules.

name: Flying Gripper
description: Cooperative modular robots that can grasp objects. Four modular quadrotors connected through magnetic hinges form a flying four-bar gripper that can grasp and transport objects.
imageAlt: Modular aerial robots forming a hinged flying gripper around an object.

name: ModQuad-Vi
description: Vision-based modular quadrotors capable of autonomous docking.

name: H-ModQuad
description: Heterogeneous modular multirotor with 4, 5, or 6 controllable degrees of freedom.

name: Catenary Robot
description: Two quadrotors connected by a cable, capable of manipulating and transporting objects.

name: PogoDrone
description: Quadrotor with a passive jumping mechanism.

name: SBlimp (Swing-Blimp)
description: Helium-assisted robot that exploits swinging dynamics for translation.

name: Aerial Hitch Robot
description: Multi-UAV cable system that forms and controls hitches for autonomous grasping and transportation.

name: MochiSwarm
description: Modular micro-blimp swarm platform for autonomous multi-robot experiments.

name: Spinning Blimp
description: Minimalist blimp using continuous rotation and passive aerodynamic surfaces for locomotion.

name: FlySurf
description: Flying deformable surface controlled by multiple aerial robots.

name: AirBender
description: Dual-UAV system for adaptive transportation of bendable objects.
